results.content:
Help Scout is a strong Zendesk alternative if your team is primarily email-based and wants an inbox that feels human rather than like traditional ticketing software, as long as you’re comfortable modeling AI resolution costs separately.

Pros:

 Shared inbox feels like a natural extension of email rather than a ticketing system
 Clean interface that new agents learn in under an hour
 Docs knowledge base included on Plus and Pro plans
 Startup and nonprofit discount programs available

Cons:

 AI Answers is billed per resolution rather than bundled into the plan
 Pro plan requires a 10-seat minimum

Pricing:

Starts at $25/user/month.

How Does Help Scout Compare to Zendesk? [...] Where things got complicated was cost. Freddy AI Copilot wasn’t included in our base plan, so once we wanted AI-assisted replies, we had to add a separate per-agent fee on top of what we already paid. The core ticketing plan was reasonably priced, but by the time we added AI and moved into the Omni line for broader channel support, the bill looked very different from the number on the pricing page.

Freshdesk is still a capable Zendesk alternative if your team wants a cloud-based tool with a large app marketplace and a lower entry price than Zendesk’s Suite plans, but budget carefully if AI is part of the plan from day one.

Pros: [...] I ran LiveAgent for an e-commerce support team that needed email, chat, and phone support without three separate subscriptions. The unified ticket view worked well, and having a built-in call center meant we didn’t need to bolt on a third-party VoIP tool just to handle phone tickets.

Where I ran into friction was social media channels. Adding Instagram support pushed us into a higher tier faster than I expected, since Instagram required Facebook as a prerequisite add-on. If your support mix is mostly email and chat, the entry plan is genuinely affordable, but channel-heavy teams should map out their needs before committing to the smallest plan.

LiveAgent is a solid Zendesk alternative for teams that want phone support bundled in without paying enterprise prices for it.

### 9. Kustomer: Best for CRM-style customer timelines

Kustomer, independent again after its Meta chapter, organizes support around the customer rather than the ticket. Every interaction lands on one chronological timeline.

Key features

 Timeline view of every customer interaction
 AI agents for automated conversations
 Omnichannel routing with skills-based assignment
 Native CRM objects and custom data

Pros: Genuine single customer view. Strong for high-volume B2C. Flexible data model.

Cons: Premium pricing. Implementation takes real effort.

Pricing: Kustomer starts at $89 per user per month.
